title: Machine Learning in Quantitative Finance
text:
Ebube Anozie
PhD Student in Applied Mathematics
University of Colorado Boulder
View the code on GitHub




This portfolio explores the application of machine learning methods to quantitative-finance problems.
Throughout the semester, I will apply statistical learning techniques to financial market data, investigate their computational properties, evaluate model performance, and interpret the results from a quantitative-finance perspective.
The project is developed as part of CSCI 5612: Machine Learning for Data Science at the University of Colorado Boulder.





Can machine-learning methods identify useful and robust patterns in financial market data?

The project investigates this question through a sequence of supervised and unsupervised learning methods.

Exploratory analysis

The project will progressively incorporate the machine-learning methods covered in CSCI 5612.

Financial markets generate large, noisy, and high-dimensional datasets. Machine learning provides a collection of tools for extracting structure from these datasets and developing data-driven models.
My broader interest lies at the intersection of:
Applied Mathematics · Machine Learning · Numerical Methods · Quantitative Finance
This project is an opportunity to explore how these areas can work together.




I am a PhD student in Applied Mathematics at the University of Colorado Boulder.
My interests include quantitative finance, machine learning, mathematical modeling, numerical methods, and computational science.
I am particularly interested in developing mathematical and computational methods for large-scale, data-driven problems.
